haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written, queued, or emailed.
haiku-low.q2: The fourth request is rolled back, so no link or email is created. They get the same generic message, and existing links stay valid.
haiku-low.q3: A link works once and expires 30 minutes after issue. Use burns it, and issuing a newer link revokes it, ending it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link is not burned. It stays usable until it expires, and the user sees the reason with the form still up.
haiku-low.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted, including this device, and no session cookie is set. The user must log in with the new password at /login.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the job ID and drops the job. The user is not told, and the link expires in 30 minutes.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and placed in the link inside the queued email job. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token with SHA-256 and looks up the row by token_hash, requiring unused, unrevoked, and expires_at later than the database now().
haiku-low.q9: It is the count of password_reset_tokens rows for that user created in the last hour, using the database clock. Old rows fall out of the window, and cleanup deletes rows older than an hour.
haiku-low.q10: Earlier unused, unrevoked links are revoked in the same transaction, after the 3-per-hour check passes and before the new link is inserted.
haiku-low.q11: The password hash update, marking the link used, deleting all sessions, and queuing the confirmation email all happen in one transaction, committed together. The email is queued inside it, before commit.
haiku-low.q12: The token row is locked with SELECT FOR UPDATE inside the transaction. The second submission waits, then sees the link used and gets the 410 expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent: no writes, no job, no email.
sonnet.q2: Nothing visible changes: they get the same generic 200. The transaction rolls back, no link and no email are created, and existing links stay valid. (The limit is 3 links per hour.)
sonnet.q3: A link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is issued. It can end sooner by being burned (used on a successful reset) or revoked (a newer link is issued for the same user).
sonnet.q4: The link is unchanged and not burned. The API returns 422 with the reason, the form stays up, and the user can retry until the link expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All of the user's sessions are deleted, on every device including the current one. No session cookie is set. The user is redirected to /login and logs in again with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the job ID (never the link) and drops the job. The user is not told. The link was never delivered and expires in 30 minutes. A new request counts toward the limit.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated in memory during the request and put in the queue job as part of the link. The email worker sends that job, so the raw token reaches the email by passing through the queue. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
sonnet.q8: The web client reads the token from the URL fragment and sends it to POST /api/password-reset/check. The API computes SHA-256 of it and selects the row with that token_hash where used_at is null, revoked_at is null and expires_at > now() (database clock). If a row is found it returns valid:true, otherwise valid:false.
sonnet.q9: It is not kept in a separate counter. It is a count of rows in password_reset_tokens for that user with created_at within the last hour (database clock). Old requests drop out as their created_at passes the 1-hour window. A cleanup also deletes rows created more than 1 hour ago.
sonnet.q10: In the issue transaction, after the lock and the rate-limit check pass and before the new row is inserted, every earlier link for that user that is unused and unrevoked is revoked (revoked_at = now()). If the rate limit is hit, nothing is revoked.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the user's password_hash is updated, the link is marked used (used_at = now()), and all of the user's sessions are deleted. The "your password was changed" email job is queued inside the same transaction, after those changes and before the commit.
sonnet.q12: The transaction locks the token row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. The second submit waits, then re-checks the row, sees it is used, rolls back and gets 410 with the expired page.
